historical_references.reference: Mawdood ibn Jabal was a companion and close friend of the Prophet Muhammad. He was one of the ten companions who were given the title 'Ashab al-Siddiq' (People of Truth). Mawdood was known for his courage and devotion to Islam. He participated in several battles with the Prophet including the Battle of Khaybar, where Muslims defeated the Jewish tribe of Banu Nadir.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, period of Prophet Muhammad's life and military conquests

historical_references.reference: Mawdood ibn Mansoor was the Umayyad Caliph who ruled the Islamic Empire from 754 to 755 AD. His reign was marked by military campaigns against the Byzantine Empire and efforts to consolidate Umayyad power in the central lands of the Caliphate. Mawdood is also known for his patronage of scholars and his construction of the Great Mosque of Damascus, which is considered a masterpiece of Islamic architecture.
historical_references.context: Late Umayyad Caliphate, period of military expansion and architectural achievements
